tracks.title: Counter Number Three
tracks.genre: Stax-style Memphis horn soul
tracks.subject: A middle-aged man named Mr. Odell buys a bottle of vitamin C he does not need every Thursday at the same pharmacy counter just to hear the pharmacist, Bernadette, say hello; after eleven bottles she writes her phone number on the receipt.
tracks.caption: Stax-style Memphis horn soul, mid-tempo shuffle groove. Tight staccato baritone sax, tenor sax and trumpet horn stabs, a gritty clean-toned Telecaster playing choppy off-beat chords, a Hammond B3 organ with light Leslie swirl, a punchy melodic bass walking under a snappy snare backbeat. 1966 Memphis studio texture, tape-warm, dry room, horns tight and forward. Male lead, warm gritty tenor, mid-high register, relaxed and grinning delivery, with a small gospel-leaning backing group answering the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 112 BPM, Bb major. Bashful, bouncy flirtation. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no synth pads, no EDM drops, no modern pop sheen.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - baritone sax and trumpet riff over Hammond and choppy guitar]

[Verse 1]
Every Thursday, half past four
Mr. Odell walks through the door
Asks for vitamin C, a bottle of ten
Third one this month and he's back again

[Pre-Chorus]
Bernadette stamps the paper bag
Says "Sir, you could stock up, you know"
He says "I like the walk, I like the line"
Looks at his shoes, he's slow to go

[Chorus]
Counter number three, counter number three
That's where my Thursday waits for me
I don't need a cure, I don't need a pill
Just one "Hello, Mr. O" and I'm well

[Verse 2]
Eleven bottles since the spring
She's kept the count of everything
Tonight she folds the receipt in two
Writes seven digits in ballpoint blue

[Pre-Chorus]
He reads it twice under the shop light hum
Walks to the door, then back he comes
Grinning wide at the counter glass
"Miss, I'll take one more of that"

[Chorus]
Counter number three, you wrote it down for me
Now Thursday's got a Friday, and a Saturday too
I don't need a cure, I don't need a pill
Just one "Hello, Mr. O" and I'm well

[Outro - horns and organ, call and response]
Thursday, Thursday, Friday's on the way
Thursday, Thursday, hey, hey, hey

tracks.title: Odd Days, Even Days
tracks.genre: baroque pop (harpsichord and strings, 1967 lineage)
tracks.subject: Sixty-year-old identical twin brothers own one old bicycle between them and ride it on alternate dates, odd days for one and even days for the other, until the 31st of the month starts an argument.
tracks.caption: Baroque pop, gentle 4/4 lilt with a walking bassline. Bright harpsichord playing broken-chord figures, a string quartet with sweeping legato cello and violin countermelodies, felt piano doubling the vocal, a solo flute answering the chorus, soft brushed snare and round electric bass. 1967 London studio texture, plate reverb, warm tape saturation, strings forward. Male lead, light clear tenor, intimate mid register, tender delivery with close double-tracked harmony on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, D major. Wistful, tender, gently comic. No drum machine, no electric guitar distortion, no synth pads, no autotune, no modern pop production.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - harpsichord figure, then cello and flute enter]

[Verse 1]
One old bicycle, two grey men
Same chin, same cough, same walk back then
Odd days Edwin, even days me
That's the deal we signed at seventy-three

[Chorus]
Odd days, even days, we take our turns
Twin of mine, I'll wait at the gate
He leaves a note in the basket each night
"Mind the left brake, it pulls to the right"

[Verse 2]
Thirty-one comes round like a bill
Whose turn is it? Neither of us will
Say it's his, so we both stand still
Two old brothers at the foot of the hill

[Chorus]
Odd days, even days, we take our turns
Twin of mine, I'll wait at the gate
I hear his bell come up the lane
My turn to wait, my turn again

[Bridge - strings alone, harpsichord rolling]
Two shadows on one wheel
Going round the way they feel

[Chorus]
Odd days, even days, we take our turns
But the thirty-first, we ride it together
Him on the saddle and me on the bar
Twin of mine, it isn't far

[Outro - flute and harpsichord, strings fade]
Odd days, even days
One bicycle, two ways

tracks.title: False Bottom
tracks.genre: Canterbury-scene jazz-rock pop (Soft Machine and Caravan lineage)
tracks.subject: A stage magician's assistant who spends every show folded into the false bottom of a trunk, counting the audience's applause from inside, decides tonight that she will take the bow before him, because the trick only works on her cue.
tracks.caption: Canterbury-scene jazz-rock pop, fluid 7/8 verses opening into straight 4/4 choruses. Warm Fender Rhodes electric piano with chromatic chord movement, a fuzz-toned electric bass playing winding melodic lines, a soprano saxophone doubling the vocal melody and trading phrases, a busy jazz drum kit with ride cymbal and snare ghost notes. Dry English 1971 studio texture, slightly woolly warm tape, Rhodes and bass forward. Female lead, plain warm alto, mid register, conversational and deadpan delivery with clean unison harmony on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 126 BPM, E minor. Dry, wry, quietly triumphant. No synth pads, no trap drums, no autotune, no big pop drops, no stadium guitar solos.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes and fuzz bass in 7/8, soprano sax enters]

[Verse 1]
I fold myself in at a quarter past nine
Knees to my chin in the lining
The velvet smells of dust and pine
I count the hands outside it

[Chorus]
False bottom, false bottom
Who's the one who makes it work
Four hundred hands above my head
And he gets to take the bow

[Verse 2]
Two taps for the card, three for the dove
One slow knock for the cue
He's waited on my hand six years
And never thanked the trunk

[Pre-Chorus]
The rabbit has his own dressing room
I get a hook and a hood
Tonight I'll let the lid go slow
And let him count the wood

[Chorus]
False bottom, false bottom
Tonight I know the way
The lid goes up when I say so
And he can wait for my cue

[Bridge - sax solo over Rhodes, groove tightens to 4/4]
The lid goes up and I stand
With the whole room in my hands

[Outro - soprano sax and Rhodes in 7/8]
Two taps for the card
One slow bow for me

tracks.title: Fresh Paste Friday
tracks.genre: UK freakbeat (1966-67 mod and psychedelic beat)
tracks.subject: A bill-poster pastes gig posters onto the same hoarding by the bus station every Friday morning and finds each one peeled off by Monday, so he starts printing an extra copy for the girl who clearly wants it on her bedroom wall.
tracks.caption: UK freakbeat, 1966-67 mod beat drive, driving 4/4 with tambourine on the off-beats. Jangling Rickenbacker twelve-string guitar, a snarling fuzz-toned lead guitar in short riffs, a Farfisa organ playing pumping chords, a punchy melodic bass, and a fast snare-heavy drum kit with crash accents. 1967 London studio texture, compressed and punchy, spring reverb, slightly raw and fast. Male lead, bright nasal tenor, mid-high register, cheeky and punchy, with group shouted backing on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 138 BPM, A major. Jaunty, cheeky, a little love-struck. No drum machine, no synth pads, no autotune, no modern pop gloss, no slow ballad sections.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - fuzz guitar riff and Farfisa, drums crash in]

[Verse 1]
Friday morning, bucket and brush
Wet paste dripping, in a rush
Stick the band to the hoarding wall
Bus station, wall to wall

[Chorus]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
Somebody takes my poster away
Fresh paste Friday, one for the wall
One for the girl I haven't met at all

[Verse 2]
I printed an extra, tucked in my coat
Rolled it up with a rubber band and a note
"Hope it's not creased, hope it's not torn
See you Friday at the bus-stop door"

[Chorus]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
Monday morning, the hoarding's grey
But there's a cup of tea on the kerb for me
And a note that says "Same time next week"

[Bridge - organ and fuzz riff]
Stick it on, hold it down
Best poster in the town

[Chorus]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
She turned up with a mug and a tray
Fresh paste Friday, one for the wall
One for the girl who came to stay

[Outro - fuzz guitar and Farfisa, crash ending]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
Fresh paste Friday, hey

tracks.title: Quarter Past Twelve in Almeria
tracks.genre: cinematic spaghetti-western ballad (Morricone-style)
tracks.subject: A stunt gunfighter at a tourist western town in the Almería desert has been shot dead at the same balcony every day at 12:15 for twenty-two years; today a small child in the crowd claps for him alone.
tracks.caption: Cinematic spaghetti-western ballad, slow 4/4 pulse with a heartbeat kick. Nylon-string and twangy tremolo electric guitar playing a slow arpeggio, a solo whistle carrying the melody, a harmonica answering, a sweeping string section with low cello, and rolling timpani with a distant church bell. Wide 1968 Rome studio texture, spacious desert reverb, spring reverb on guitar, dry intimate vocal. Male lead, deep warm baritone, low-mid register, slow and weathered, with a small male choir humming softly on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 70 BPM, D minor. Dusty, solemn, quietly proud. No drum machine, no synth pads, no autotune, no rock drum kit, no modern pop beat.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - whistle over tremolo guitar, timpani heartbeat]

[Verse 1]
Noon in Almería, the tourists come
Sit on the rail with ice cream and drum
I put on the hat and the dusty black coat
Check the cap gun, check the rope

[Chorus]
Quarter past twelve, the shot goes off
I spin, I stagger, I give a cough
They clap for the hero, they clap for the pay
Nobody claps for the man who stays

[Verse 2]
A crack in the plank where my shoulder lands
Sand in my collar, sand in my hands
My knees say no, my pride says yes
Twenty-two years in the same black vest

[Pre-Chorus]
Today a small boy in a paper hat
Stands on a bench, says "Look at that"
He doesn't clap for the man with the gun
He claps for me, the fallen one

[Chorus]
Quarter past twelve, the shot goes off
I spin, I stagger, I give a cough
One little pair of hands, one little sound
Tells a dead man he's still around

[Bridge - strings swell, whistle alone]
I lie in the dust with my hat on my chest
And for once I do not want to rest

[Outro - whistle and harmonica, strings fade, bell]
Quarter past twelve
Quarter past twelve

A harmonium plays the lilting main melody, a gambus doubles it with plucked ornaments, marwas hand drums and a tambourine drive a bouncy two-beat dance rhythm, a violin answers each line, no drum kit. [Intro - harmonium, marwas]

[Verse 1]
Bang Mamat masuk toko wangi di Blok M
Hidungnya mampet dari bulan Agustus
Mbak penjual nyodorin botol satu-satu
Bang Mamat nyengir, kagak ada yang kecium

[Pre-Chorus]
Mbak, bilangin aja deh
Wanginya kayak apa

[Chorus]
Kata Mbak ini kayak mangga abis ujan

Ane kagak ngerti, ane percaya aja

Di rumah Neng Lastri ia sodorin botol

Persis kata Mbak toko, Bang Mamat kaget
Padahal itu kata Mbak toko semua

[Chorus]
Kata Neng ini wangi mangga abis ujan
Bang Mamat ketawa, hidungnya masih mampet
Ane kagak ngerti, ane percaya aja
Yang wangi tuh Neng, bukan cuma botolnya

[Outro - violin, harmonium]
Bungkusin dua, bungkusin dua
Biar Neng seneng hati

tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - hasapi, sulim]

[Verse 1]
Di bazar buku bekas perpustakaan Balige
Kubeli novel tua seribu rupiah
Di kantong belakangnya ada kartu tanggal
Satu nama berulang, Tigor Sihombing

[Pre-Chorus]
Buku kedua, namanya sama
Buku ketiga, tulisannya sama

[Chorus]
Siapa kau, Tigor, yang baca duluan
Kau tandai halaman yang kutandai juga
Kupinjam semua yang pernah kau pinjam
Mungkin di rak mana kita berpapasan

[Verse 2]
Ibu pustakawan tersenyum, ia tahu orangnya
Katanya Tigor mengajar di Laguboti
Kutulis satu surat, kuselip di kartu
Tanggal kembali kuisi minggu depan

[Chorus]
Siapa kau, Tigor, yang baca duluan
Hari ini kubalik halaman yang sama
Kupinjam satu lagi, kuselip suratku
Semoga kau yang membukanya berikutnya

[Outro - sulim, hasapi]
Tanggal kembali, minggu depan
Mungkin kita bertemu di situ

[Intro - tsugaru shamisen and taiko, hand claps]

[Verse 1]
弘前の裏通り 二階の彫り師の店
十円玉ほどの りんごを入れたい

ばあちゃん笑って 針を持ち上げる

[Pre-Chorus]
いち にい さん し
三味線の拍で数えな

昼休みのうちに戻る 課長にはばれたくない

ちくっとちくっと じょんがら節

あと十回で 終わりだよ
歯を食いしばるな 歌いなよ

[Chorus]
ちくっとちくっと じょんがら節
腕のりんごを 見てごらん
ちくっとちくっと じょんがら節
明日は袖を まくって行こう

[Outro - shamisen and taiko, fade]

tracks.subject: Every Sunday morning a retired husband secretly pencils wrong answers into the Thai crossword his wife fills in with a black pen, just so she will look up and scold him.
tracks.caption: Thai khrueang sai chamber pop (saw duang, khim and khlui). saw duang high-pitched fiddle with sweet bowed tone, khim hammered dulcimer in rippling figures, khlui bamboo flute with breathy long notes, krap wooden clappers marking the beat. small-room acoustic recording, warm natural reverb, gentle and unhurried. male lead, soft warm mid-range voice, gently sung, light female harmony joining in the chorus. [Intro - khim ripples, saw duang melody, khlui]

เช้าวันอาทิตย์ ข้าวต้มยังร้อน
เธอนั่งกับปากกาหมึกดำ

tracks.subject: A Phú Thọ tea-picker's son flies a paper kite fitted with a bamboo flute so it hums over the tea hills; the girl picking on the next hill ties a red scarf to her own kite tail and tugs back, until the two strings tangle.
tracks.caption: Phu Tho hat gheo folk-pop sung in Vietnamese, flirtatious call-and-response. Breathy bamboo sao truc flute lead, dan nhi two-string fiddle answering each phrase, lightly strummed acoustic guitar, small trong com hand drum, upright bass walking gently. Airy open room, natural acoustic mix. Male and female duet trading lines, bright mid-range, clearly sung with a light folk lilt. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 104 BPM, D major. Teasing, sunny, shy-flirty mood. No rapping, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no EDM drop, no distorted guitar, no vocal effects.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - sao truc, dan nhi]

[Verse 1]
Diều anh gắn sáo thổi trên đồi chè
Gió chiều lùa qua, tiếng vang xuống xóm
Em hái chè xanh, nón nghiêng che mặt
Nghe tiếng sáo diều, tay em chậm lại

[Pre-Chorus]
Ai thả diều đấy, ghẹo em đấy à
Dây diều anh giật, lòng em cũng giật

[Chorus]
Ới a diều sáo, kêu thêm tiếng nữa
Em đứng đồi bên, em nghe rõ cả
Anh thả dây dài qua ba luống chè
Em giật dây lại, xem anh có buông

[Verse 2]
Chị em trong đội trêu em đỏ mặt
Bảo diều ai thổi mà em ngẩn ngơ
Em buộc khăn đỏ lên đuôi diều giấy
Gửi sang đồi bên, coi anh nhận không

[Chorus]
Ới a diều sáo, kêu to hơn nữa
Anh nhìn khăn đỏ, anh chạy qua đồi
Hai sợi dây diều quấn vào nhau mãi
Em giật dây lại, anh chẳng chịu buông

[Bridge - dan nhi, trong com]
Gỡ sao cho ra, ai cũng không gỡ
Thôi để vậy luôn, chiều nay chưa về

[Chorus]
Ới a diều sáo, hát tiếp đi nào
Hai con diều chung một đồi chè
Mai anh sang nhà, mang sáo hay mang trầu
Em giật dây lại, em chẳng buông đâu

[Outro - sao truc, dan nhi]
Ới a diều sáo
Hai dây quấn nhau
